sources.title: Stress and the brain: from adaptation to disease
sources.authors: de Kloet ER, Joëls M, Holsboer F
sources.used_for: MR/GR dual-receptor theory; HPA-hippocampus interaction framework; MR high affinity (Kd~0.5nM) vs GR low affinity (Kd~5nM); master switch concept
sources.notes: Core reference for MR/GR balance theory. Authors are field founders. Heavily cited.

sources.title: Stress effects on the hippocampus: a critical review
sources.authors: Kim EJ, Pellman B, Kim JJ
sources.used_for: Three-level stress effects (behavioral/neural/structural); biphasic LTP (low CORT→MR→enhanced, high CORT→MR+GR→impaired); hippocampus vs amygdala directional divergence; human PTSD hippocampal volume correlation
sources.notes: Full text read via PMC. Comprehensive integration of multiple labs' data.

sources.title: Chronic stress-induced hippocampal vulnerability: the glucocorticoid vulnerability hypothesis
sources.used_for: Glucocorticoid vulnerability hypothesis (modification of Sapolsky's cascade); CA3 dendritic retraction time course (4 days persistent, 10 days recovery); reversibility; enhanced neurotoxic vulnerability mechanism; sex differences; Cushing's/PTSD/MDD clinical parallels
sources.notes: Full text read via PMC. Key paper for distinguishing vulnerability (reversible structural change) from neurodegeneration (irreversible cell death).

sources.title: Hippocampal fast glutamatergic transmission is transiently regulated by corticosterone pulsatility
sources.authors: Sarabdjitsingh RA, Pasricha N, Smeets JAS, Kerkhofs A, Mikasova L, Karst H, Groc L, Joëls M
sources.used_for: Non-genomic rapid signaling: first corticosterone pulse increases mEPSC frequency and AMPA receptor surface expression within minutes; pulsatile vs tonic hormone effects; ultradian rhythm importance
sources.notes: Full text read via PMC. PLoS ONE in vitro hippocampal culture. Single lab. Mechanism directly relevant to rapid non-genomic LTP enhancement.

sources.title: Depression duration but not age predicts hippocampal volume loss in medically healthy women with recurrent major depression
sources.authors: Sheline YI, Sanghavi M, Mintun MA, Gado MH
sources.used_for: Human evidence: cumulative depression duration (not age) predicts hippocampal volume loss; dose-response relationship between glucocorticoid burden and structural damage
sources.notes: Full text read via PMC. MRI study n=62. Landmark human evidence for GC-mediated hippocampal atrophy in depression.

sources.title: Glucocorticoids are critical regulators of dendritic spine development and plasticity in vivo
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
sources.used_for: In vivo two-photon imaging: corticosterone increases dendritic spine turnover dose-dependently within 5 hours; MR/GR receptor specificity for spine formation vs elimination
sources.notes: Full text read via PMC. In vivo real-time spine dynamics. Strongest causal evidence for rapid GC effects on synaptic structure.

sources.title: The neuroendocrinology of stress and aging: the glucocorticoid cascade hypothesis
sources.authors: Sapolsky RM, Krey LC, McEwen BS
sources.used_for: Original formulation of glucocorticoid cascade hypothesis: hippocampal damage → impaired HPA feedback → rising GCs → further damage
sources.notes: Seminal 1986 paper. Abstract only. Historical significance for the cascade framework.

sources.title: Physiology and neurobiology of stress and adaptation: central role of the brain
sources.used_for: Allostatic load concept; structural remodeling in hippocampus/amygdala/PFC; social support and exercise as protective interventions
sources.notes: Abstract only. Comprehensive McEwen review. Core for allostasis concept.

sources.title: Cortisol levels during human aging predict hippocampal atrophy and memory deficits
sources.authors: Lupien SJ, de Leon M, de Santi S, Convit A, Tarshish C, Nair NP, Thakur M, McEwen BS, Hauger RL, Meaney MJ
sources.used_for: Human longitudinal evidence: elevated cortisol over 5 years → reduced hippocampal volume + memory deficits in aging humans
sources.notes: Abstract only. Landmark Nature Neuroscience paper. Closest human evidence for cortisol → atrophy → memory impairment chain.

sources.title: Learning under stress: how does it work?
sources.authors: Joëls M, Pu Z, Wiegert O, Oitzl MS, Krugers HJ
sources.used_for: Temporal and spatial specificity principle: stress enhances LTP only when stress hormones act on circuits active during learning at the time of learning
sources.notes: Abstract only. Key paper for the bidirectional stress-memory relationship. Central citation for the 'why stress can help' section.

sources.title: The stressed hippocampus, synaptic plasticity and lost memories
sources.used_for: Amygdala-hippocampus directional divergence under stress: stress impairs hippocampal LTP/memory while enhancing amygdalar fear memory; integrates GC/CRH/catecholamines
sources.notes: Abstract only. Nat Rev Neurosci landmark review. Essential for the amygdala-hippocampus imbalance section.

sources.title: Tau as the Converging Protein between Chronic Stress and Alzheimer's Disease Synaptic Pathology
sources.used_for: Chronic GC exposure → tau missorting → synaptic atrophy; mechanism connecting chronic stress to AD via tau pathway
sources.notes: Abstract only. Rodent models. Single lab. Tau mechanism hypothesis connecting stress and AD.
